Definition: COVID-19 symptom assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published when-to-get-help guidance.
FirstAid: Call Qatar 999 now, help the person sit in the easiest breathing position, use a mask only if tolerated and it does not impede breathing, and do not allow self-driving. Follow the call-handler's instructions. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Are sudden throat or tongue swelling, wheeze, faintness, or collapse the main concern rather than an infection developing over time?
questions.Information: Sudden systemic allergic-reaction features require the Anaphylaxis pathway.

questions.Question: Does the person seem very unwell or getting worse, have sudden chest pain, is so breathless they can't say short sentences at rest, are they coughing up blood, or have they collapsed, fainted, or had a first-time seizure, or developed a non-fading rash?
questions.Information: NHS.UK COVID-19 guidance lists these as call-999/A&E criteria.

questions.Question: Without an emergency feature, is there worsening breathlessness, persistent fever or dehydration, oxygen saturation below the locally approved threshold, or is the patient an infant, pregnant/postpartum, older/frail, immunocompromised, or living with significant chronic disease?
questions.Information: Higher-risk patients and worsening respiratory or hydration symptoms need prompt assessment, including eligibility for time-sensitive treatment under current Qatar policy.

questions.Question: Are symptoms mild and improving in an otherwise low-risk older child or adult, with normal breathing, hydration and alertness, and none of the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance recommends rest, fluids, and simple pain relief for mild COVID-19, with isolation guidance to protect others.

advice.Title: Emergency respiratory precautions
Content: Call Qatar 999 now, help the person sit in the easiest breathing position, use a mask only if tolerated and it does not impede breathing, and do not allow self-driving. Follow the call-handler's instructions. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: worsening breathing, blue/grey colour, collapse, confusion, or loss of consciousness.

advice.Title: Prompt Qatar COVID-19 assessment
Content: Use the current Qatar governance-approved in-person or telehealth pathway. Confirm current testing, isolation, antiviral eligibility, oxygen thresholds, pregnancy, pediatric and immunocompromise policy; this UAT protocol must not hard-code changing public-health rules.
Call Back If: breathing worsens, oxygen falls, chest pain, confusion, poor intake, reduced urine, or collapse.

advice.Title: Home care for mild COVID-19
Content: Rest, drink plenty of water, take paracetamol or ibuprofen if uncomfortable, and try honey for cough (not for babies under 12 months). Stay away from others per local isolation guidance. Avoid lying flat while coughing.
Call Back If: breathing difficulty develops; symptoms significantly worsen.

references: NHS.UK, "COVID-19 symptoms and what to do", https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/covid-19/covid-19-symptoms-and-what-to-do/ (page last reviewed 21 March 2023)
